issues.issue: The parenthetical "(including its subsidiaries, collectively identified herein as \"BSC\")" leaves it uncertain whether every BSC subsidiary is a contracting party bound by, and entitled to enforce, the confidentiality obligations. The execution date is also left blank/illegible on the face of the instrument.

The "Project" is defined by the specific example of "Orbus' coronary R. stent platform" followed by the open catch-all "and other stent products", leaving the outer reach of the defined term genuinely uncertain. Because the use restriction is measured by the Project, the boundary of that catch-all is exactly what parties would fight over.

The only definition of the operative term "Project" sits in a WHEREAS recital, while the operative use restriction (c008: use "solely for the purpose of evaluating the mutual interests of the Parties in the Project") depends on it, raising a recital-versus-operative-text problem.

"Information" is defined open-endedly ("including but not limited to ... and physical observation"), but the enumerated specifics could be read to limit the catch-all. The tension is mild because the definition is deliberately broad and is narrowed downstream by the designation requirements.

Protection turns on Information "which a Party desires to protect" — a purely subjective and unmeasurable criterion — coupled with designation "in the manner provided by this Agreement". Whether the desire, the designation, or both are required is genuinely open.

The cross-reference to designation "in the manner provided by this Agreement" points to c005, whose sentence has no operative verb, so the required manner of designation cannot be fixed from the instrument as a whole.

The lead-in sentence "All Information which is disclosed by one Party to the other Party and which is to be protected hereunder as Proprietary Information of the disclosing Party." is a fragment ended by a period, with no predicate connecting it to sub-paragraphs (a) and (b). Whether labelling/identification is a condition precedent to protection, or merely a housekeeping step, turns on repairing that mechanical error.

Read against the definition in c004, which protects Information a Party merely "desires to protect", this clause would require conspicuous marking or written confirmation within thirty business days, leaving unmarked disclosures unresolved between the two provisions.

The care standard is "the same degree of care with which it treats its own Proprietary Information of like character", an internal and unmeasurable benchmark, and the five-year clock runs "from the date of disclosure" rather than from any fixed date. Both leave room for competing readings of when protection lapses.

This clause sets an internal-practice standard of care while the immediately following warranty in c007 promises "reasonable safeguards", an objective standard; the two measures of the same duty are not obviously reconcilable.

"Reasonable safeguards" is undefined and no benchmark is supplied, and the clause is cast as a present-tense "warrants that it applies" rather than a covenant, blurring whether it is a representation or an ongoing obligation.

The objective "reasonable safeguards" warranty sits against the subjective standard in c006 ("same degree of care with which it treats its own"), so which standard governs a breach claim is unresolved.

"Solely for the purpose of evaluating the mutual interests of the Parties in the Project" gives no boundary to what counts as evaluation, and "the Project" is itself defined only by an open-ended recital. This is the clause on which a misuse dispute would turn.
The permitted purpose is tied to "the Project", a term defined nowhere in the operative text but only in the WHEREAS recital (c002), so the operative restriction depends for its scope on a recital.

The exception list is mechanically broken: the first two exceptions carry no letters while the last two are labelled (c) and (d), and the permitted-recipient phrase ("employees and consultants ... in the consideration or evaluation of the Project") is garbled to the point that the class of authorized recipients cannot be fixed. The trailing "unless and until such time as" also leaves unclear whether the exceptions qualify the disclosure ban or the whole obligation.

The operative words are missing — "Except as expressly provided herein, ___ is granted by either Party to the other Party" contains no subject (presumably "no license") — and the enumeration "any patent, patent application, trademark, copyright" simply stops with no closing catch-all. Whether trade secrets or know-how are covered cannot be answered from the text.

"Upon any termination of this Agreement and/or at the written request and instruction of the disclosing Party" uses "and/or", leaving unclear whether return is automatic on termination or only on demand, and the "one archival copy" carve-out is silent on how long that copy may be kept or used.

The clause is triggered by "any termination of this Agreement", but the instrument contains no term or termination provision at all — only the five-year protection period in c006 — so the triggering event is undefined by the contract read as a whole.

A merger clause limited to "the subject matter hereof" invites argument about how far it displaces other dealings between BSC and Orbus, but no competing integration or prior-agreement provision appears in this instrument.
